# Veslo Automations Managed Skill Implementation Plan

> **For Claude:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.

**Goal:** Build persistent Veslo Automations so Veslo agents can create one-shot and recurring automations through a managed locked user-global skill and an official server-backed tool/API.

**Architecture:** Add a first-class automation domain, durable store, server runner, and workspace API in `packages/server`. Expose the API to the Veslo agent through a managed OpenCode plugin/tool generated by desktop internal provisioning, and ship a managed locked user-global `veslo-automations` skill through the existing managed materialization path. Migrate the Automations UI from raw scheduler jobs toward the new API while keeping existing scheduler jobs as a compatibility source.

**Tech Stack:** Bun/TypeScript Veslo server, SolidJS shared app shell, Tauri desktop provisioning, WebdriverIO desktop E2E, existing skill registry/materialization infrastructure, OpenCode plugin `tool()` APIs.

---

## Preconditions

- Work in a fresh branch/worktree, for example `codex/veslo-automations-managed-skill`.
- Keep the existing dirty worktree changes out of this implementation branch unless the user explicitly asks to include them.
- Use @test-driven-development for implementation steps.
- Use @systematic-debugging for failures.
- Use @verification-before-completion before claiming done.
- Do not use `packages/web`, raw Vite, or `pnpm -w dev:ui` as the runtime proof.
- If `packages/server/src` changes, run `pnpm --filter openwork-server build:bin` before desktop/runtime validation.

```ts
import { expect, test } from "bun:test";

import {
  computeNextAutomationRunAt,
  parseAutomationSchedule,
  parseAutomationStatus,
} from "./automations.js";

test("parses one-shot schedule with ISO runAt", () => {
  const schedule = parseAutomationSchedule({
    kind: "oneShot",
    runAt: "2026-06-06T07:00:00.000Z",
    timezone: "Europe/Prague",
  });

  expect(schedule).toEqual({
    kind: "oneShot",
    runAt: "2026-06-06T07:00:00.000Z",
    timezone: "Europe/Prague",
  });
});

test("computes next one-shot run only before completion", () => {
  const schedule = parseAutomationSchedule({
    kind: "oneShot",
    runAt: "2026-06-06T07:00:00.000Z",
  });

  expect(computeNextAutomationRunAt(schedule, Date.parse("2026-06-05T07:00:00.000Z"))).toBe("2026-06-06T07:00:00.000Z");
  expect(computeNextAutomationRunAt(schedule, Date.parse("2026-06-07T07:00:00.000Z"))).toBe("2026-06-06T07:00:00.000Z");
});

test("computes daily and weekly next run times", () => {
  expect(computeNextAutomationRunAt(
    { kind: "daily", hour: 9, minute: 0, timezone: "Europe/Prague" },
    Date.parse("2026-06-05T06:00:00.000Z"),
  )).toBe("2026-06-05T07:00:00.000Z");

  expect(computeNextAutomationRunAt(
    { kind: "weekly", weekday: 1, hour: 9, minute: 0, timezone: "Europe/Prague" },
    Date.parse("2026-06-05T06:00:00.000Z"),
  )).toBe("2026-06-08T07:00:00.000Z");
});

test("computes cron next run in timezone", () => {
  expect(computeNextAutomationRunAt(
    { kind: "cron", expression: "0 9 * * 1-5", timezone: "Europe/Prague" },
    Date.parse("2026-06-05T08:30:00.000Z"),
  )).toBe("2026-06-08T07:00:00.000Z");
});

test("rejects invalid schedule and status payloads", () => {
  expect(() => parseAutomationSchedule({ kind: "oneShot", runAt: "tomorrow" })).toThrow("schedule.runAt");
  expect(() => parseAutomationSchedule({ kind: "interval", seconds: 10 })).toThrow("schedule.seconds");
  expect(() => parseAutomationSchedule({ kind: "cron", expression: "" })).toThrow("schedule.expression");
  expect(() => parseAutomationStatus("unknown")).toThrow("status");
});
```

**Step 3: Implement minimal domain code**

Create `packages/server/src/automations.ts` with these exported types and helpers:

```ts
export type AutomationSchedule =
  | { kind: "oneShot"; runAt: string; timezone?: string }
  | { kind: "cron"; expression: string; timezone?: string }
  | { kind: "interval"; seconds: number }
  | { kind: "daily"; hour: number; minute: number; timezone?: string }
  | { kind: "weekly"; weekday: number; hour: number; minute: number; timezone?: string };

export type AutomationStatus = "active" | "paused" | "completed" | "failed" | "cancelled";
export type AutomationRunStatus = "queued" | "running" | "success" | "failed" | "skipped";

export type AutomationTarget = {
  preferredSessionId?: string;
  fallbackTitle?: string;
  agent?: string;
  model?: string | null;
  variant?: string | null;
};

export type VesloAutomation = {
  id: string;
  workspaceId: string;
  name: string;
  enabled: boolean;
  status: AutomationStatus;
  schedule: AutomationSchedule;
  prompt: string;
  target: AutomationTarget;
  createdAt: string;
  updatedAt: string;
  nextRunAt?: string | null;
  completedAt?: string | null;
  lastRunId?: string | null;
};

export type AutomationRun = {
  id: string;
  automationId: string;
  scheduledFor: string;
  startedAt?: string | null;
  finishedAt?: string | null;
  status: AutomationRunStatus;
  sessionId?: string | null;
  createdSession: boolean;
  error?: string | null;
};
```

Implement:

- `parseAutomationSchedule(value: unknown): AutomationSchedule`
- `parseAutomationStatus(value: unknown): AutomationStatus`
- `parseAutomationRunStatus(value: unknown): AutomationRunStatus`
- `computeNextAutomationRunAt(schedule: AutomationSchedule, fromMs: number): string | null`
- `isValidIsoInstant(value: string): boolean`
- `normalizeTimezone(value: unknown): string | undefined`

Use `cron-parser` for cron expressions. Keep daily/weekly/interval behavior deterministic and covered by tests.

Store path:

```ts
join(workspaceRoot, ".opencode", "veslo", "automations.json")
```

Migration rules:

- If the new file exists, read only the new file.
- If the new file is missing but legacy Agent Lab file exists, convert legacy items into `VesloAutomation`.
- Convert `interval`, `daily`, and `weekly` schedules directly.
- Use `workspaceId` from the active route/config, not from the legacy record.
- Set `status` to `active` when enabled, otherwise `paused`.
- Preserve `lastRunAt` and `lastRunSessionId` by creating a synthetic successful run record when present.
- Do not delete the legacy file during migration.

## Task 3: Add Automation Runner With Restart Recovery

**Files:**
- Create: `packages/server/src/automation-runner.ts`
- Create: `packages/server/src/automation-runner.test.ts`
- Modify: `packages/server/src/automation-store.ts`
- Modify: `packages/server/src/automations.ts`

**Step 1: Write failing runner tests**

Create tests with injected clock/timers and a fake executor.

Cover:

- runner schedules active future one-shot automations on start
- due one-shot within 24-hour grace window runs after restart
- stale one-shot older than grace window becomes skipped
- successful one-shot becomes `completed`
- recurring automation computes the next future occurrence after success
- duplicate scheduled occurrence does not run twice
- missing preferred session path records `createdSession: true`

Expected runner API:

```ts
const runner = createAutomationRunner({
  workspaces: [{ id: "ws_1", path: workspaceRoot }],
  now: () => currentMs,
  setTimeout: fakeSetTimeout,
  clearTimeout: fakeClearTimeout,
  execute: async (input) => ({
    sessionId: input.target.preferredSessionId ?? "ses_new",
    createdSession: !input.target.preferredSessionId,
  }),
});
```

Run:

```bash
pnpm --filter veslo-server test automation-runner.test.ts
```

Expected: FAIL.

**Step 2: Implement runner API**

Create:

```ts
export type AutomationExecutionInput = {
  workspaceId: string;
  workspaceRoot: string;
  automation: VesloAutomation;
  scheduledFor: string;
  target: AutomationTarget;
  prompt: string;
};

export type AutomationExecutionResult = {
  sessionId: string;
  createdSession: boolean;
};

export type AutomationRunner = {
  start(): Promise<void>;
  stop(): void;
  refreshWorkspace(workspaceId: string): Promise<void>;
  runNow(workspaceId: string, automationId: string): Promise<AutomationRun>;
};
```

Implementation notes:

- Keep all timer handles in memory; never treat timers as source of truth.
- Read persistent store before scheduling each workspace.
- Use stable run IDs: `run_${automation.id}_${Date.parse(scheduledFor)}` with non-alphanumeric characters normalized.
- Write a `running` record before executing.
- Write `success`, `failed`, or `skipped` terminal records.
- On one-shot `success`, set automation `status` to `completed`, `enabled` to false, and `completedAt`.
- On recurring `success`, keep `active` and compute next `nextRunAt`.
- On due startup recovery, run if `now - scheduledFor <= 24h`; otherwise write skipped.
- Do not replay every missed recurring occurrence; process at most one due occurrence on startup and then compute next future time.

**Step 3: Start runner from `startServer`**

In `startServer(config)`:

- Create the runner before `Bun.serve`.
- Start the runner after `Bun.serve` is created.
- Wrap `server.stop` so tests and desktop shutdown clear timers.

Example shape:

```ts
const automationRunner = createAutomationRunner({
  workspaces: config.workspaces,
  execute: createOpenCodeAutomationExecutor(config),
});
const routes = createRoutes(config, approvals, tokens, automationRunner);
const server = Bun.serve(serverOptions);
void automationRunner.start().catch((error) => console.error("[veslo-automations] runner failed", error));
const originalStop = server.stop.bind(server);
(server as typeof server & { stop: typeof server.stop }).stop = (closeActiveConnections?: boolean) => {
  automationRunner.stop();
  return originalStop(closeActiveConnections);
};
```

Adjust to Bun's actual `stop` signature.

```ts
export const VESLO_AUTOMATIONS_SKILL_NAME = "veslo-automations";

export function vesloAutomationsSkillMarkdown(): string {
  return `---
name: veslo-automations
description: Create persistent Veslo automations, reminders, follow-ups, recurring checks, and delayed tasks through the Veslo Automations API.
---

# Veslo Automations

Use when the user asks Veslo to remind them, run something later, repeat a task, monitor something, create a daily or weekly check, or schedule an action.

Always use the Veslo automation tools:
- veslo_create_automation
- veslo_list_automations
- veslo_run_automation
- veslo_update_automation
- veslo_delete_automation

Do not create raw cron jobs, launchd jobs, systemd timers, shell scripts, or direct OpenCode scheduler jobs.

Decision rules:
- One future execution: create oneShot.
- Repeated cadence: create daily, weekly, interval, or cron.
- Ambiguous time: ask one concise clarification question.
- Default to the current workspace and current session.
- After creating, verify by reading the automation back and tell the user the next run time.
`;
}
```

## Definition Of Done

- Veslo server exposes the official Automations API.
- Automations persist under `.opencode/veslo/automations.json`.
- One-shot automations survive restart and become `Completed` after success.
- Recurring automations compute the next run without replaying an unbounded backlog.
- Preferred session is reused when available; otherwise a new same-workspace session is created.
- Veslo agent has native automation tools and a managed locked user-global skill telling it when and how to use them.
- Users cannot modify or delete the managed skill through normal local skill editing/removal flows.
- Automations UI uses the new API as the primary source.
- Server, app, and desktop E2E checks pass against the real Tauri runtime.
